'''Bernd Fischer''' (18 December 1936 – 13 August 2020) was a German [[mathematician]].

He is best known for his contributions to the classification of finite [[simple group]]s, and discovered several of the [[sporadic group]]s. He introduced [[3-transposition group]]s and constructed the three [[Fischer group]]s, predicted the existence of the [[Baby monster group|baby monster]] and [[monster group]]s, and described and computed the [[character table]] of the baby monster.

He did his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1963 at the [[Johann Wolfgang Goethe University of Frankfurt am Main]] under the direction of [[Reinhold Baer]].<ref>[https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=26741 The Mathematics Genealogy Project - Bernd Fischer<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref><ref>{{cite book
  | last = Ronan
  | first = Mark
  | authorlink = Mark Ronan
  | title = Symmetry and the Monster, One of the Greatest Quests of Mathematics
  | publisher = [[Oxford University Press]]
  | year = 2006
  | isbn = 0-19-280722-6 }}</ref>

== Career ==
Fischer went to Goethe University in Frankfurt to study mathematics under Baer in the early 60s, receiving his PhD in 1963. He later moved to the [[Bielefeld University]], where he became head of mathematical sciences. 

In 1970, he classified the almost-simple groups generated by [[3-transposition group|3-transpositions]]. In the process, he discovered three new [[Sporadic group|sporadic groups]], which were later called the [[Fischer group|Fischer groups]]. His proof that the classification was complete was known but not published in a single narrative until [[Michael Aschbacher|Aschbacher]] published an elementary introduction of 3-transposition groups in 1996.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Aschbacher|first=Michael|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/3transposition-groups/4718F16418EB5A2431BB421D83ED7579|title=3-Transposition Groups|date=1996|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-521-57196-8|series=Cambridge Tracts in Mathematics|location=Cambridge}}</ref>

By loosening some of the conditions on his classification, in 1973 he predicted the existence of two larger sporadic simple groups: a {3,4}-transposition group, now known as the [[Baby monster group|baby monster]] group, and a {3,4,5,6}-transposition group now known as the [[Monster group|monster]] group or the [[Fischer-Griess Monster]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Griess|first=Robert|date=December 14, 2020|title=My life and times with the sporadic simple groups|url=https://cmsa.fas.harvard.edu/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/sporadic-life-article-14dec2020-submitted.pdf|url-status=live|access-date=December 12, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210126202422/https://cmsa.fas.harvard.edu/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/sporadic-life-article-14dec2020-submitted.pdf |archive-date=2021-01-26 }}</ref>  These would turn out to be the two largest sporadic groups that could exist. [[Robert Griess]] independently discovered the Monster group and published a description in 1976.<ref>{{cite book| last = Griess | first = Robert L. | year = 1976
 | title = Proceedings of the Conference on Finite Groups (Univ. Utah, 1975)
 | editor1-last = Scott | editor1-first = W. Richard
 | editor2-last = Gross | editor2-first = Fletcher
 | publisher = [[Academic Press]] | location = Boston, MA
 | pages = 113–118
 | isbn = 978-012633650-4 | mr = 0399248}}</ref>

Fischer went on to compute the character table for both monsters, in collaboration with Donald Livingstone and Michael Thorne.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-08-26|title=Bernd Fischer|url=https://robwilson1.wordpress.com/2020/08/26/bernd-fischer/|access-date=2021-12-28|website=Hidden assumptions|language=en}}</ref> Leon and Sims first produced a construction of the baby monster in 1977,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Leon|first1=Jeffrey S.|last2=Sims|first2=Charles C.|year=1977|title=The existence and uniqueness of a simple group generated by {3,4}-transpositions|url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.bams/1183539473|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|volume=83|issue=5|pages=1039&ndash;1040|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1977-14369-3|doi-access=free|authorlink2=Charles Sims (mathematician)}}</ref> and Griess produced one for the monster in 1980.

== Personal life ==
Fischer was raised in [[Bad Endbach]].  He later moved to [[Werther, North Rhine-Westphalia|North Rhine-Westphalia]], where he died in August, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-08-24|title=The man behind the Monster {{!}} Mark Ronan|url=https://thecritic.co.uk/the-man-behind-the-monster/|access-date=2021-12-28|website=The Critic Magazine|language=en-GB}}</ref>
